Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: Caucasian woman with insulin-dependent diabetes and hypertension
Age: 51 years

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient was admitted with a perimesencephalic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) in the prepontine, interpeduncular, ambient, and crural cisterns. She had a previous SAH due to a 6mm aneurysm in the anterior communicating artery (Acomm), which was treated with endovascular coiling.

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient's hospital course was complicated by vasospasm and cerebral salt wasting. She was treated with hypervolemia, hypertension, intra-arterial nicardipine, and sodium and volume supplementation. After discharge, she returned to work with no residual neurologic deficits.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
N/A

FOLLOW-UP:
The patient had a follow-up magnetic resonance imaging and angiography performed six months later, which demonstrated no vascular abnormalities.

CONDITION AT DISCHARGE:
The patient was discharged home in good condition on post-bleed day 10.

text:
# Principal diagnosis: I60.8 Other subarachnoid haemorrhage

This is a coding judgement. The discharge diagnosis section was withheld, so it should be confirmed against the full record.

## Why I60.8

- **The bleed is non-traumatic SAH.** That places the code in I60.
- **The bleed pattern is perimesencephalic.** The blood sits in the prepontine, interpeduncular, ambient and crural cisterns, around the brainstem. That pattern typically means a non-aneurysmal, presumed venous bleed.
- **Imaging found no vascular source.** Follow-up MRI and angiography at 6 months showed no abnormality.
- **No specific artery code fits.** Codes I60.0–I60.7 need a bleed from an identified artery, such as the carotid siphon, MCA, ACom or PCom. None was identified for this episode, but the bleed has a defined, recognised pattern. That makes I60.8 more fitting than I60.9 (unspecified).

## Why not I60.2 (anterior communicating artery)

The earlier Acomm aneurysm was a separate, prior event and was already treated with coiling. The current bleed's distribution and the negative angiography do not support re-rupture. If the clinician had documented coil failure or re-bleeding from that aneurysm, I60.2 would apply instead.

## Possible additional codes

These depend on documentation and local coding standards. Verify exact codes against the current ICD-10-AM edition.

- Cerebral vasospasm, as a complication of the SAH
- Cerebral salt wasting, as a sodium disorder (E87.1 if hyponatraemia is documented)
- Type 1 or insulin-treated diabetes (E10.x / E11.x, as documented)
- Hypertension (I10)
- History of the coiled aneurysm (Z86.7- / Z95.- range, as applicable)
